The supplied model has unequal opposing force arrows. Which conclusion about balance follows from their relative lengths and directions?

  1. unbalanced; the opposing arrows do not represent equal force magnitudes, so the net force is nonzero
  2. balanced because any two opposite arrows always cancel even if their lengths differ
  3. unbalanced only because the object is moving
  4. no forces act because a force diagram cannot show balanced forces

choices.text: unbalanced; the opposing arrows do not represent equal force magnitudes, so the net force is nonzero
balanced because any two opposite arrows always cancel even if their lengths differ
unbalanced only because the object is moving
no forces act because a force diagram cannot show balanced forces

canonical_seed.solution_text: Balanced forces have a zero vector sum; unequal opposing forces give a nonzero net force.

canonical_seed.answer: A correct diagram has weight downward, support upward, pull to the right, friction to the left. It should not include forces that the sled exerts on other objects, and it should not use a velocity arrow as a force.
